sop.coo_evaluation:
**Gaps — no SOP yet**

• **Member Onboarding** – no standardised first-touch process; inconsistent induction quality likely driving early churn
• **Member Checkins** – no documented cadence or trigger points for retention conversations (30/60/90 day, post-pause, low attendance)
• **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back protocol, exit interview process, or data capture on *why* members leave
• **Coaching Development Roadmap** – coaches promoted/hired with no clear progression, skill benchmarks, or capability gaps identified
• **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no systematic review of coaching delivery, class energy, or member experience consistency
• **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – no clarity on non-class duties (1-to-1s, programming, member feedback, admin) or accountability
• **Member data privacy & GDPR** – critical gap; no documented handling of personal data, consent, retention, or incident response
• **Complaints & Incidents** – no formal log, resolution SOP, or escalation path for member or staff complaints

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## REVENUE — BIGGEST PRIORITY: FIX CHURN & REV/MEMBER COLLAPSE

**The problem:** Sept is your best absolute month (£22,016, 168 members) but revenue *per member* has crashed to £131 — down from £145 in July and £139 in April. You're adding members but each one generates less cash. That's a pricing or mix problem, not a volume win.

• **Audit your membership tiers right now.** You're likely signing too many new members on intro/discount rates or lower-tier plans. Sept added 15 net members (153→168) but rev/member fell 10%. Either lock new joiners onto full price after 3 months, or shift the new-member offer from price cuts to 1-to-1 PT sessions (upsell, not discount).

• **Attack the May churn spike (12.8%) — it's your outlier.** Post-Easter lull? Summer holidays starting? Identify the cohort that churned and test a targeted retention play (e.g. free July class pass, partner discount, accountability challenge). Keeping just 2–3 of those lost members would add £250+/month ongoing.

• **Upsell class packs + PT to your growing base.** You've got 168 active members; unlimited membership alone isn't scaling revenue fast enough. Launch a tiered upsell: beginner PT block (4 sessions, £80), advanced class pass add-on (8 sessions, £60). Target 20% attachment in Q4 — that's +£1,500/month with near-zero marginal cost.

---

## EXPENSES — DATA GAP, BUT FLAG STAFFING INTENSITY

• **You haven't given me cash-out figures.** Pull September payroll, rent, utilities and supplier costs from Starling. My instinct: at £22k revenue and 168 members, if payroll is >40% of revenue you're overstaffed for this scale — most boutique gyms run 28–35%. If rent/rates is >15%, the relocation isn't paying off yet and you need to hit 200+ members to breakeven on the new space.

• **Direct supplier (laundry, cleaning, towels, equipment maintenance).** These scale with headcount. Audit Q3 vs Q2 spend — should be flat or 2–3% higher, not 10%+. If they've drifted up, renegotiate or switch suppliers before Q4.

---

class_stats.suggestion:
**For quiet studio time between PT and classes:**

1. **Open-gym blocks on Friday/Saturday mornings** — your quietest days with low baseline traffic. Offer 60-90 min slots (6am-7:30am Friday, 9am-10:30am Saturday) at a reduced walk-in rate or included for members; this builds habit and fills the studio when it's otherwise empty.

2. **Pay-per-use PT block on Thursday evenings** — Thursday is your third-quietest day. Reserve 30-min slots at a lower rate than standard PT (e.g., €30 instead of €50) for members wanting form checks or targeted work, marketed as "drop-in coaching."

**To lift the quietest classes:**

3. **Reschedule Capacity and Barbelle to Tuesday/Wednesday mornings at 6:30am or 7am** — your peak days. These classes are so underattended they have room to float. Test them in high-traffic windows for 4 weeks; if attendance doesn't lift, they may need a format review, but the slot change is the first lever. Pair with a targeted email to your Tuesday/Wednesday regulars explaining what these classes offer differently from Build classes.

kpis.Action: INTERNAL: Create clear service menu (for coaches and for members) — what we offer, what it costs, what's included.
kpis.advice:
# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your delivery reality, not your wishes**
Map what your coaches *actually deliver right now* — not what you plan to offer in six months. Audit 3-4 typical member journeys this week. Document: class types, one-on-one formats, nutrition check-ins, progress tracking, whatever's real. This becomes your honest baseline menu.

**2. Price by value extraction, not cost-plus guessing**
Don't calculate "hourly rate × hours." Instead: interview 5-8 members who've paid for premium add-ons (extra PT sessions, nutrition plans, challenges). What problem did they solve? What would they *have paid* for it? Price the *outcome*, not the time. This justifies premium tiers your coaches can actually sell.

**3. Create TWO separate menus with different language**
**Coach menu** = operational (what they deliver, duration, prerequisites, upsell triggers). **Member menu** = benefit-driven (what you'll achieve, who it's for, what's included vs. add-ons). Members don't care about your process; they care about their result. The coach version drives accountability; the member version drives conversion.

**4. Test and lock it in writing within 7 days**
Get draft versions into your coaches' hands. Ask: "Can you sell this? Is anything missing?" Revise once. Publish as a simple one-pager (PDF, printed laminate for the gym floor). Ambiguity kills sales — specificity moves inventory.

**5. Build your first upsell path into the menu itself**
Show the base offer, then explicitly show what *one step up* looks like

Map what your coaches *actually deliver right now* — not what you plan to offer in six months. Audit 3-4 typical member journeys this week. Document: class types, one-on-one formats, nutrition check-ins, progress tracking, whatever's real. This becomes your honest baseline menu.

**2. Price by value extraction, not cost-plus guessing**
Don't calculate "hourly rate × hours." Instead: interview 5-8 members who've paid for premium add-ons (extra PT sessions, nutrition plans, challenges). What problem did they solve? What would they *have paid* for it? Price the *outcome*, not the time. This justifies premium tiers your coaches can actually sell.

**3. Create TWO separate menus with different language**
**Coach menu** = operational (what they deliver, duration, prerequisites, upsell triggers). **Member menu** = benefit-driven (what you'll achieve, who it's for, what's included vs. add-ons). Members don't care about your process; they care about their result. The coach version drives accountability; the member version drives conversion.

**4. Test and lock it in writing within 7 days**
Get draft versions into your coaches' hands. Ask: "Can you sell this? Is anything missing?" Revise once. Publish as a simple one-pager (PDF, printed laminate for the gym floor). Ambiguity kills sales — specificity moves inventory.

**5. Build your first upsell path into the menu itself**
Show the base offer, then explicitly show what *one step up* looks like
